MoSPI unveils new CPI series covering more items and services, with revised weights

# Page 4^page=4
Understanding The Consumer Price Index (CPI) is a measure of movement of prices of goods and services that households purchase for the purpose of consumption over time. The Base Year is a chosen year taken as a reference point (index = 100) to compare prices over time. The previous series had a base year of 2012 and was based on consumption expenditure patterns of 2011-12. The base year of the new CPI series is 2024=100.

# Page 5^page=5
The item basket and the corresponding weights are based on Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24. 36.75% 17.66% 8.80% 6.38% 6.10% 5.04% 4.47% 3.61% 3.35% 3.33% 2.99% 1.52% 0% 5% 10% 15% 20% 25% 30% 35% 40% Food and beverages Housing, water, electricity, gas and… Transport Clothing and footwear Health Personal care, social protection and… Furnishings, household equipment and… Information and communication Restaurants and accommodation services Education services Paan, tobacco and intoxicants Recreation, sport and culture Weights of CPI Combined 2024(%) The base year of the new CPI series is 2024=100. The latest Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2023-24 is used for updating item basket and weights of CPI 2024 series.

# Page 6^page=6
Shift from a 6-group structure to a more detailed 12-division structure The change in structure between both the series is due to adoption of COICOP 2018 Framework of UNSD.

# Page 7^page=7
Major Update The Ministry plans to institutionalize base revisions at regular intervals. As per global practices, it should be done every three to five years, depending on the availability of Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) data. Index reference period: It is the period for which index equals 100. For the current CPI, the index reference period is 2024=100. Price reference period: It is the period during which the base prices are collected. The price reference for the current CPI series is calendar year 2024. Weight reference period: It is the period for on the basis of which weights are calculated. For CPI 2024, Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24 data is used for deriving the weights.

Summary Feature Old Series New Series (Feb 2026 Onward) Base Year 2012 = 100 2024 = 100 Weight Source Consumer Expenditure Survey (2011–12) Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (2023–24) Total Items Tracked 299 (259 goods, 40 services) 358 (308 goods, 50 services) Food & Beverage Weight 45.86% 36.75% Housing & Fuel Weight 10.07% (Housing only) 17.67% (Combined with water, electricity, fuel) + Rural Housing The previous CPI series with base 2012=100 served as a stable and reliable measure for more than a decade; however, during this period, significant structural changes have occurred in consumption behaviour, income levels, urbanisation, expansion of the services sector and digitalization.

Index of Industrial Production (IIP) is defined as a summary measure that measures the changes in the volume of industrial production of a representative basket of industrial products during a particular period with respect to a chosen base period. The IIP for the base period is taken as 100 and that for the study period shows the percentage increase or decrease over the base period.

Q1. With reference to the newly introduced CPI series (Base 2024 = 100), consider the following statements: 1. The expenditure weights in CPI 2024 are derived from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey (HCES) 2023–24. 2. The new series adopts the Classification of Individual Consumption According to Purpose (COICOP) 2018 framework, replacing the earlier six-group structure with a 12-division structure. 3. The number of weighted items at the all-India level has decreased compared to the CPI 2012 series. 4. Rural house rent has been included for the first time to improve coverage of rural housing consumption. Which of the above statements are correct? A. 1 and 2 only B. 1, 2 and 4 only C. 1, 3 and 4 only D. 2 and 3 only E. 1, 2, 3 and 4 MCQs for Practice
